svg.aria-label: The 55 registered tools split into 26 local, 22 remote and 7 mixed. Local tools run live because replaying a periodogram would let the task author rather than the data decide what the model got wrong. Remote tools are always replayed because every one opens a socket. Mixed tools are decided per call from the arguments. The classification is closed: an unclassified tool raises.
svg.title: The 55 registered tools split into 26 local, 22 remote and 7 mixed. Local tools run live because replaying a periodogram would let the task author rather than the data decide what the model got wrong. Remote tools are always replayed because every one opens a socket. Mixed tools are decided per call from the arguments. The classification is closed: an unclassified tool raises.
svg.text: 55 REGISTERED TOOLS, OVER 21 MODULES
26 local
22 remote
CLASS L — RUN LIVE
Local and deterministic: they read the
bundled fixture tree and compute.
Replaying a periodogram would let the
task author, not the data, decide
whether a model's mistake is visible.
CLASS R — ALWAYS REPLAYED
Every one opens a socket, so none is
ever executed inside a benchmark run;
each is replayed from a recorded
fixture. Includes one that merely looks
local: get_literature_cluster_params.
CLASS M — DECIDED PER CALL
Local code behind a network-capable
argument. A task must pin the offline
path in the call's own arguments
(use_field_cal=false; catalog_fixture
with compare_to) or it is replayed.
The plane is closed: an unclassified tool raises rather than defaulting, and a test asserts it covers the whole registry.
A new registry tool must be classified in the same commit that adds it — otherwise the first new remote tool runs live, inside a run that believes it is offline.
